title: Choose Portivane's visual world
question: Choose the operator-console direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Fiber Route Tray
options.lineage: fiber splice trays and optical route maps
options.thesis: Every published service is one bright, inspectable route from localhost to hostname.
options.viewport: A left service rail feeds one oversized route canvas showing local port, tunnel edge, and public hostname on a continuous line.
options.risk: The route graphic must remain operational rather than becoming decoration.

raised.raise: Status uses line weight, dash, and doubling so color is never the only signal.
Connection phases change the whole route field's light level, not scattered badges.
Accent color stays confined to live route edges and never floods the workspace.
Secondary data packs tightly into ruled strips without inflating into cards.

options.label: Rack Faceplate
options.lineage: homelab rack labels and patch panels
options.thesis: The machine becomes a labeled rack where every open port can be patched to the public internet.
options.viewport: Listening ports form a compact rack at left while the selected service opens as a broad patch bay with a single publish lever.
options.risk: It is highly familiar to homelab users but can exclude people who have never handled network hardware.

options.label: Living Terminal
options.lineage: green-phosphor terminal in a midnight machine room
options.thesis: Tunnel setup unfolds as a legible keyboard-first conversation with the machine.
options.viewport: A continuous transcript records discovery, login, DNS, and connection while the next valid command waits at the bottom.
options.case: Strong audience recognition, but command language makes the beginner workflow less immediately clear.
options.risk: The interface may feel like the command line the product is meant to simplify.

options.label: Route Departure Board
options.lineage: segmented boarding pass and live gate board
options.thesis: Services queue as departures, and publishing assigns each one a live public gate.
options.viewport: A fixed-column service board reranks active routes while a selected route expands into a segmented publishing pass.
options.case: The origin-to-destination mapping is exceptionally clear, though less culturally native to self-hosting.
options.risk: Travel language can become cute if labels stop using real networking terms.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: Every service registers as a precise spectral line on one calibrated network rail.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail carries listening ports, active routes, and the selected hostname.
options.case: Precise but too abstract for users learning what a tunnel does.
options.risk: Requires a legend before the core action becomes obvious.
options.kept: Status remains legible through line form without relying on hue.

options.label: Connection Dawn
options.lineage: theatrical cyclorama from blackout to day
options.thesis: A tunnel moves the workspace from local night through connecting dawn to public daylight.
options.viewport: The connection state occupies a broad horizon with controls arranged as labeled lighting cues.
options.case: Connection phases are memorable, but the system hides multiple simultaneous services.
options.kept: Connection state changes the environmental light level as one coordinated event.

options.label: Diffracted Cloud Edge
options.thesis: A narrow spectral edge reveals which local service has become publicly reachable.
options.viewport: A quiet service field gains a narrow iridescent route edge only when a tunnel becomes live.
options.case: The Cloudflare association is immediate, but the operational model is too implicit.
options.risk: It can drift into generic cloud-software softness.
options.kept: Color is confined to the active edge while content remains achromatic.

options.label: Dense Utility Mosaic
options.thesis: Ports, routes, logs, and controls share one compact ruled mosaic with no wasted pixel.
options.viewport: A tight CSS grid places every discovered port and tunnel state above the fold.
options.case: Experienced operators scan it quickly, but first-time users face too much at once.
options.risk: Density can obscure the one-click publishing promise.
options.kept: Secondary information uses compact ruled strips rather than repeated floating cards.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar infrastructure dashboard with sidebar navigation, status cards, and a tunnel table.
canonCard.viewport: A sidebar frames account status, summary cards, a services table, and a New tunnel button.
canonCard.risk: Immediately understandable but visually interchangeable with other admin tools.
